# syq 0.9.0

This release lets a server copy files from your laptop with its approval,
gives copies between two other servers a single approval per copy, makes
receiving services switch to new versions more reliably, and fixes the
findings of a security review.

## Highlights

- `syq cp --from @laptop PATH` on a server copies files from your laptop. The
  laptop shows the exact paths and asks every time.
- A copy between two other servers started on a third one is approved once on
  your laptop and runs on the source server, which connects to the destination
  directly. The requesting server no longer gets access to either account.
- After an update, `persist` commands switch idle receiving services right
  away, approved account connections no longer hold the old version, and a
  switch keeps the login it checked so receiving can't drop out.
- Reruns remove the partial files an interrupted copy left behind (Linux local
  filesystems).
- Clearer approval prompts and several hardening fixes for receiving, updates
  and the wire protocol.

## Compatibility changes

SSH authorization providers can no longer approve direct copies between two
servers; use `--auth-from @NAME`, or `--coordinate-at local` to copy through
the requesting server. Connections syq keeps open after a command, including
`syq ssh` with persistence on, no longer forward your SSH agent or configured
port forwards; use `ssh -A` when you need forwarding. New `--into` directories
follow the destination's umask. Old `syq-copy-worker-` lines in
`~/.ssh/authorized_keys` grant nothing and can be deleted.

The matching Python package is published after the native release.

See the [0.9.0 changelog](https://github.com/greaber/syq/blob/v0.9.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete behavior changes, compatibility notes and fixes.
